payload.prompt: El cliente Marta Weber SL (org. nº 852274118) tiene una factura pendiente de 45700 NOK sin IVA por "Asesoría de datos". Registre el pago completo de esta factura.

payload.goal: Registrar el pago completo de 45700 NOK (sin IVA) de la factura pendiente de 'Asesoría de datos' del cliente Marta Weber SL.
success_checks: Cliente Marta Weber SL (org. nº 852274118) existe en el sistema
Factura por 'Asesoría de datos' de 45700 NOK con IVA 0% está creada y en estado 'pendiente'
Pago completo de 45700 NOK registrado contra la factura
Factura queda en estado 'pagada' (PAID) tras el registro
risk_notes: El sandbox está vacío: se debe crear el cliente, el pedido, las líneas de pedido y la factura antes de registrar el pago
No se especifica fecha de factura ni fecha de pago; se usará la fecha actual por defecto
No se especifica cuenta bancaria de destino; se debe configurar o verificar una cuenta bancaria activa
IVA explícitamente 0% (sin IVA / sin mva); vat_rate_percent=0 confirmado
No se indica número de factura existente; se asume que debe crearse en el flujo previo
No se especifica método de pago (transferencia, efectivo, etc.); puede requerir selección manual
payload.suggested_first_action: Crear el cliente Marta Weber SL con org. nº 852274118 mediante POST /customer
ordered_steps: 1. POST /customer — Crear cliente 'Marta Weber SL' con org. nº 852274118
2. GET /bank/account — Verificar o configurar cuenta bancaria activa para recibir pagos
3. POST /order — Crear pedido asociado al cliente Marta Weber SL
4. POST /order/{orderId}/orderline — Añadir línea 'Asesoría de datos', cantidad 1, precio 45700 NOK, IVA 0%
5. PUT /order/{orderId}/invoice — Generar factura a partir del pedido
6. GET /invoice — Verificar que la factura está en estado 'UNPAID' con importe 45700 NOK
7. POST /invoice/{invoiceId}/payment — Registrar pago completo de 45700 NOK con fecha actual
8. GET /invoice/{invoiceId} — Confirmar que el estado de la factura es 'PAID'

planned_endpoints.summary: Find accounts corresponding with sent data.
Create customer. Related customer addresses may also be created.
Find products corresponding with sent data.
Create order line. When creating several order lines, use /list for better performance.
Create invoice. Related Order and OrderLines can be created first, or included as new objects inside the Invoice.
Find payment type corresponding with sent data.
Update invoice. The invoice is updated with payment information. The amount is in the invoice’s currency.
Find vouchers corresponding with sent data.
Reverses the voucher, and returns the reversed voucher. Supports reversing most voucher types, except salary transactions.
Find invoices corresponding with sent data. Includes charged outgoing invoices only.

rules: Use params={"number": XXXX} to resolve a specific account number to its ID.
This is a QUERY PARAM via the params field — NOT json_body.
Do NOT use /ledger/accountingPeriod — it does not exist.
For bank account setup: isBankAccount=true, bankAccountNumber='12345678903', bankAccountCountry={"id": 161}.
MUST include id and version from the GET response.
When email is provided, ALWAYS set BOTH email AND invoiceEmail to the same value.
Do NOT send isCustomer (it's readOnly and auto-set).
For addresses, use postalAddress={addressLine1, postalCode, city, country={id: 161}} for Norway.
ALWAYS search first if product_number is provided: GET /product?number=<number> — sandbox pre-seeds products.
Only POST /product if GET returns 0 results.
Use 'number' field for the product number (NOT productNumber).
priceExcludingVat sets the base price. Also set vatType={"id": 3|5|6}.
Requires customer={"id": customer_id}.
Set orderDate and deliveryDate (use today_iso from execution_brief).
When a product was created, ALWAYS include product={"id": product_id} on the orderline.
Use unitPriceExcludingVatCurrency for the price field.
Set vatType={"id": 3} for 25%, {"id": 5} for 15%, {"id": 6} for 0%.
For multiple lines, prefer POST /order/orderline/list for efficiency.
Pass orders=[{"id": order_id}] to link order.
Set invoiceDate and invoiceDueDate.
Bank account 1920 MUST be configured first (see bank account setup pattern).
Method is PUT, not POST.
ALL params are QUERY PARAMETERS — NOT in body: PUT /invoice/{id}/:payment?paymentDate=YYYY-MM-DD&paymentTypeId=XXXXX&paidAmount=YYYYY
Do NOT send a JSON body — send empty body or no body. ALL data goes in the URL query string.
Get paymentTypeId first via GET /invoice/paymentType — use the first result's id.
paidAmount is the full payment amount (e.g., 47200). For foreign currency, use paidAmountCurrency instead.
REQUIRES dateFrom and dateTo as query params. Without them you get 422.
dateTo is EXCLUSIVE — if you want vouchers from March 22, use dateTo=2026-03-23 (next day).
NEVER use dateFrom == dateTo — it always returns 422. Always set dateTo = dateFrom + 1 day minimum.
Example for single day: params={"dateFrom": "2026-03-22", "dateTo": "2026-03-23"}
Example for broad range: params={"dateFrom": "2026-01-01", "dateTo": "2026-12-31"}
These are QUERY PARAMS via the params field — NOT json_body.
Method is PUT, not POST.
date is a QUERY PARAMETER: PUT /ledger/voucher/{id}/:reverse?date=YYYY-MM-DD
Do NOT send date in the request body.
ALWAYS include invoiceDateFrom and invoiceDateTo as query params — they cannot be null.
Example: GET /invoice with params={"invoiceDateFrom": "2025-01-01", "invoiceDateTo": "2026-12-31", "customerId": customer_id}.

payload.text:
Let me analyze the task:

1. Create customer "Marta Weber SL" with org number 852274118
2. Set up bank account 1920
3. Create order for the customer
4. Create order line: "Asesoría de datos", qty 1, price 45700 NOK, VAT 0%
5. Create invoice from the order
6. Get payment type
7. Register full payment of 45700 NOK

Following the trace template, I need to:
1. GET /ledger/account?number=1920 (already have ref and version from sandbox_context)
2. GET /invoice/paymentType


3. PUT /ledger/account/{id} to configure the bank account
4. POST /customer to create Marta Weber SL
5. POST /order, then POST /order/orderline for the data advisory service
6. POST /invoice and PUT /invoice/{id}/:payment to record the full payment

I can parallelize the account setup and payment type lookup since they're independent, and I already have the account reference from sandbox_context, so I'll skip the initial GET and move straight to the PUT.

Now I'm running the customer creation, account configuration, and payment type lookup all in parallel since they don't depend on each other.

Looking at this task, I need to:
1. Set up bank account 1920 (not yet configured per sandbox_context)
2. Create customer Marta Weber SL
3. Get payment type
4. Create order → orderline → invoice → payment

I'll start with the three independent calls in parallel:
